label: PF Backlog 429
title: A3: PF platform build->package->deploy + compiled packaging + signing + SBOM/LBOM + NO-RAW-.py gate (absorbs BI-PF-0383)
body: [A3] One-time rebuildable pipeline: Nuitka (Python) + go build (Go) -> signed package + SBOM/LBOM; release gate = no readable source. Includes build-time plug/unplug.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing core/packaging.py to orchestrate a two-toolchain build pipeline: Nuitka for Python modules and go build for Go core. Add signing step via core/signing.py. Add SBOM/LBOM generation during packaging. Add a NO-RAW-.py release gate as a new gate function in core/code_quality_gate.py or core/run_quality_gate.py. Wire build-time plug/unplug via config/plugins-registry.json flags consumed by build_manager. Expose through existing /api/v1/packaging/build and /api/v1/packaging/editions endpoints.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0397 (EAP manifest) to have a defined schema so the build pipeline can emit an EAP as its output artifact
RELATED BI-PF-0388 (ADR: compiled artifacts) as the governing architectural decision
RELATED BI-PF-0387 (delivery baseline) as the policy input
RELATED BI-PF-0390 (EPIC A) as the parent epic
BI-PF-0393 (absorbed) should be marked as superseded/absorbed by this item
conflict_findings: BI-PF-0397 also modifies /api/v1/packaging/manifest and core/artifact_registry.py; coordinate so the EAP output from this build pipeline matches the EAP schema from 0397
core/signing.py may also be touched by license/entitlement work in EPIC A; check for concurrent edits
config/plugins-registry.json may be edited by other plugin-related items; serialize edits
duplication_findings: core/packaging.py already provides packaging logic; extend rather than create a new pipeline module
core/signing.py already exists and should handle signing; do not duplicate
core/code_quality_gate.py, core/pr_gate.py, core/merge_gate.py already implement gate patterns; the NO-RAW-.py gate should follow the same pattern
BI-PF-0387 (delivery baseline) defines the policy; this item implements it—avoid duplicating policy text in code comments
BI-PF-0383 (build-time plug/unplug) is absorbed; its scope should be fully folded in, not re-implemented separately
analysis.rationale: Existing packaging.py, signing.py, and gate modules provide clear extension points. The pipeline orchestration is additive. Not a new component because the build, signing, and gate responsibilities are already distributed across existing modules; this item wires them into a coherent pipeline.
assumptions: Nuitka is the chosen Python compiler (per BI-PF-0388/0387)
Go core source exists or is being developed in parallel under EPIC A
CI pipeline has or can obtain Nuitka and Go toolchains
Signing uses an existing key management system or core/signing.py already abstracts this
EAP manifest (from 0397) provides the list of artifacts to compile/package
Build-time plug/unplug is controlled via config/plugins-registry.json flags consumed at build time
risks: Nuitka compilation may not cover all Python edge cases (dynamic imports, eval); need a fallback or exception list
go build and Nuitka toolchain availability in CI is an assumption; may require new CI images
Signing key management and rotation are non-trivial operational concerns
SBOM/LBOM generation adds build time; performance impact on packaging pipeline
Build-time plug/unplug (absorbed BI-PF-0383) may require deep changes to import structure
evidence: core/packaging.py, core/signing.py, core/code_quality_gate.py listed as candidate existing code
BI-PF-0388 and BI-PF-0387 establish the compiled-artifact policy
BI-PF-0383 explicitly scoped as absorbed by this item
missing_info: Is Go core source already committed, or is it a deliverable of this item?
Signing key infrastructure: existing or to be built?
Which Python modules are exempt from Nuitka compilation (if any)?
What does the release gate look like as a CI step—blocking merge or blocking release only?
Where is the NO-RAW-.py gate enforced: at build time or as a post-build check on the package contents?

missing: Go core source status (committed or to be built)
context_review.reason: Existing packaging.py, signing.py, and gate modules provide clear extension points. The missing items are operational and policy decisions, not architectural blockers.

dependencies.required_state: EAP manifest schema approved and validator implemented

brief.problem: PF must be packaged as a compiled, signed artifact with no readable source, from a one-time rebuildable pipeline.
brief.what_adds: A3 — build->package->deploy pipeline: compiled packaging (Nuitka for Python + go build for Go) + signing + SBOM/LBOM + a no-raw-.py release gate. Absorbs BI-PF-0383 (build-time plug/unplug of the worker subsystem per edition).
brief.why: IP protection (no readable source) + supply-chain integrity (signing, SBOM/LBOM) + one source -> many editions.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

objective: A3 — build->package->deploy pipeline: compiled packaging (Nuitka for Python + go build for Go) + signing + SBOM/LBOM + a no-raw-.py release gate. Absorbs BI-PF-0383 (build-time plug/unplug of the worker subsystem per edition).
acceptance_criteria: release gate fails if a raw .py is shipped
approach: Wire a rebuildable pipeline that compiles Python (Nuitka) and Go (go build), signs, emits SBOM/LBOM, and fails the release gate if any raw .py is present; exclude the worker subsystem per edition at build time.
verification: release gate fails if a raw .py is shipped

api_impact.reason: no API surface declared in backend_capability
